title: the archive.
subtitle: the map. the letter is the voice.

pages.heading: on the desk.
body: This book is not the letter.
The letter is the thing that had to be said in one sitting, in one voice, without a way back into the fog.
These pages are only the map of the same night. Notes from the same desk. The same lamp. The same rain.
If you found this, you can put it back. Nothing here needs an answer.

pages.heading: the floor.
body: Intensity is easy. It arrives like weather and leaves like weather.
The floor is the Tuesday. The same person in the morning as in the dark. The line that does not move when it would be convenient to move it.
Warmth without a floor is a truce. A truce is not a home.
I did not learn this in time to keep from hurting someone. I learned it in time to stop abandoning myself.

pages.heading: the fog.
body: Fog is not distance. Fog is closeness that will not tell the truth.
You can live in it for a long time and call it patience. You can call it love. You can call it giving space.
It is none of those. It is the refusal to pick up what is already on the floor.
Leaving the fog is not the same as leaving a person. It is the same as staying in the room as yourself.

pages.heading: without losing my humanity.
body: The work was never to become someone colder.
The work was to stop disappearing, stop chasing, stop managing a heart as if it were a project — and still remain kind.
To tell the truth without turning it into a weapon.
To leave a door open onto reality, and not stand in the doorway forever.
That is the whole archive, underneath every page. The letter is just the part that had a name.
